Instructor bio:
Patrick King is a Brooklyn based painter. He grew up in Racine, Wisconsin, still the subject of much of his work. He studied at Minneapolis College of Art and Design, Philadelphia College of Art, and Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts. He has taught at The Art Students League of New York, Temple University and Philadelphia University as well as several art centers in addition to conducting private plein air workshops.
King’s work is in numerous private and public collections. He has exhibited at the National Academy of Design, The Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts, Watercolor USA, Springfield Art Museum, American Watercolor Society, F.A.N. Gallery, Delaware Center for the Contemporary Arts, Maryland Federation of Art, Philadelphia Art Alliance, Silvermine Guild Arts Center, Gross McCleaf Gallery, and Woodmere Art Museum, among others. events.description:
Industry City and Get It Right Music in association with Murmrr Presents are happy to present a stacked triple bill including Sloppy Heads, Chris Forsyth’s What is Now, and Wet Tuna!
Event Info
Date: October 17th, 2026
Doors: 3:00pm
Show: 4:00-7:00pm
Tickets: $15 per person plus fees
The first 50 people to buy tickets get a free 12-ounce beer, well drink, 6 ounce wine or N/A beverage.
Address: Industry City Bandshell Stage, Courtyard 1/2 at Industry City in Brooklyn New York between 36th and 37th street and 2nd and 3rd Avenues.
ENTER 238 36th Street, Brooklyn, NY on your GPS device
The venue is located in an open-air courtyard featuring a full concert sound stage. Fans can get affordable drinks from the venue’s bar and order food from over 17 options inside the adjoining food hall. Concert is rain or shine.
How to get here:
Take the D, N, R lines to 36th street station in Brooklyn and walk west one block to Industry City. 3 stops from Manhattan. 30 minutes from Herald Square.
From Long Island, take the LIRR to Atlantic Terminal then take the D, N or R train to 36th street.
More about the bands:
THE SLOPPY HEADS!
Thrill to the electrifying guitar wizardry of Jimmy Jumpjump!
Gasp at the audacity of the legendary Ariella Stok aka Starmaiden to whom shame is but a word in the dictionary!
Grope to the exotic jungle rhythms of Bill the Drummer!
In one of their sought after East Coast appearances since the release of their second album, Sometimes Just One Second on Shrimper Records.
Bop on down to see them perform live in concert, where anything can happen and usually does. Fun for kids from 2 to 82.
Chris Forsyth’s WHAT IS NOW is a new collaborative project from Philadelphia guitarist Chris Forsyth (BASIC, Solar Motel Band) featuring double bassist John Moran (Bark Culture, Daniel Villareal Trio) and drummer Joey Sullivan (Florry, Bark Culture).
Together they create spontaneous song forms exploring lyrically ambient moods, repetition, rhythmic interplay, and a mindful leaderless-ness. As suggested by the players’ pedigrees, elements or motorik propulsion, trance jazz, and deconstructed rock moves abound.
The Bandcamp- and merch table-only CD “Both / And” is the debut release, about which Laura Snapes wrote this in the Guardian: “The Philadelphia guitarist swaps his usual Television-indebted questing riffage for 25 minutes of tingly, exploratory improv alongside double bassist John Moran and drummer Joey Sullivan: imagine a scruffier Necks.”
WET TUNA was formed for all beings. Legendary DJ/HEAD Jeff Conklin says “revel in the earth/space magic!” Their new record is called “VAST”. Matt “MV” Valentine with Jim Bliss & Erika Elder are the triad. They specialize in homegrown dubwise song exploration.
The kaleidoscopic sonic agriculture of Wet Tuna has long inhabited its own universe. Over the past five years, they have established themselves as one of the most forward thinking and anarchic of the many groups rethinking and reconceptualizing the notion of the “jam band,” all the while frustrating critical attempts to slot the group’s music into any scene, sound, or easily classifiable genre fad.
There remains a beautiful simplicity at the core of MV’s workbench alchemy; as with the music of Can, there is in his productions almost always a lodestar fixed within the eye of whatever maelstrom or fragmented primal abstractions surround it. On Warping All By Yourself, funk and soul are both the unifying principles and the unlikely bedrocks upon which everything else orbits and rests, resulting in a concoction of iconoclastic, free-dancing music that has as much in common with Funkadelic as it does Crazy Horse.

events.title: My Cousin Vlad & Balkan Comedy Night
events.description: Eastville Comedy Club is Brooklyn's oldest comedy clubGet ready for an unforgettable night of comedy as international comedy sensation My Cousin Vlad brings his wildly popular, high-energy stand-up show to North America.Macedonian-Australian comedian My Cousin Vlad has built a massive international following with millions of views across social media, earning fans with his razor-sharp observations, unforgettable characters and hilarious takes on family, culture and everyday life.Vlad's comedy draws from his experiences growing up in a Balkan immigrant family in Australia and the hilarious collision between old-school traditions and modern life. From marriage, kids and chaotic family gatherings to tradie culture, corporate life, building a duplex and the characters you meet along the way, Vlad turns the everyday into fast-paced, brutally funny stand-up.His unique style blends clever storytelling, spot-on impressions, quick improvisation and sharp observational comedy into a show that feels distinctly Balkan while remaining relatable to audiences from every background.Whether he's poking fun at Balkan traditions, navigating modern Australian life or exposing the universal insanity of family, My Cousin Vlad delivers an authentic, unpredictable and uniquely hilarious comedy experience.The night also features Balkan Comedy Night founder Ryan Radusinovic, who has been featured on CBS, Amazon Prime, Just For Laughs and the Netflix Is a Joke Festival. His comedy blends animated storytelling, pitch-perfect impressions, clever observations and merciless roasts. Ryan has opened for Bill Burr, Yannis Pappas, Cedric the Entertainer and Pablo Francisco, and currently tours with Jack Jr.

Bowl of ‘Zole Brooklyn Returns: 30+ Chefs, Pozole and 300 Agave Pours.
Thirty-plus kitchens. More than 300 pours of agave and regional Mexican spirits. One steaming bowl of pozole after another. On Thursday, October 22, Bowl of ‘Zole returns to Brooklyn’s Industry City for a four-hour deep dive into classic Mexican cuisine and cultura líquida—and for anyone in the food, beverage, or hospitality business, it’s a rare chance to taste where Mexican dining in New York is heading next.
This isn’t a generic tasting event. The 2026 lineup stacks James Beard Foundation nominees, Michelin-recognized restaurants, and StarChefs Rising Stars winners alongside independent neighborhood kitchens from across the five boroughs. That mix—celebrated names and under-the-radar operators under one roof—is exactly what makes grassroots festivals like this a working scouting trip for operators, buyers, and beverage directors.

Comedy kicks starts the weekend off with a bang featuring NYC's best comedians! FEATURING SPECIAL GUEST COMEDIANS...(remainder of lineup coming soon)FeaturingJames MatternPreston GitlinLauren CocroftGreg MellyJohn BennettCesh ReyesJames Mattern is a nationally headlining comic and media personality, who has quickly become one of the most beloved emcees in New York. James has released two albums, "No Segues" in 2019 and "The Check Spot" in 2021, the latter of which debuted at #1 on iTunes Comedy Charts and was voted Interrobang’s “Album of the Year” in 2021. The development of "The Check Spot" album was recorded from its conception and later released as a documentary film by the same name on YouTube on June 3, 2021.James has warmed up audiences on a number of TV shows in both New York and Los Angeles, including Netflix’s "Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj," ABC’s "The View," NBC’s "Bring the Funny," Netflix’s "The Break with Michelle Wolf," and ABC’s "The Chew." He has also appeared on PlutoTV’s "Kevin Hart Presents Comedy in Color," MSG Network’s "The Bracket," Manhattan Neighborhood Network’s "Chris Gethard Presents," Fox Sports "One's Garbage Time with Katie Nolan," WWE Network's "The List," and MSG Network’s "People Talking Sports," to name a few.Currently, James can be heard as a co-hosts "The SDR (Sex, Drugs, and Rock & Roll) Show" on G.A.S. Digital.Preston Gitlin is a New York-based stand-up comic who dreamed of being a comedian since early childhood. At age 19, he opened for Dane Cook. In his 20s, he built multiple international businesses. His first venture was in Costa Rica, where he became fluent in Spanish. The bilingual comedian also founded comedywire.com, the world’s largest comedy writing site. He has written jokes for some of the biggest celebrities, CEOs and politicians, and was honored to contribute to the 2020 Gridiron Club Dinner. He has been featured multiple times on SiriusXM, Fox Business and Bloomberg. Preston is open about his life-long struggle with anxiety and uses his comedy to help support mental health initiatives. In 2019, he launched The Mental Health Comedy Tour in partnership with TWLOHA (To Write Love on Her Arms), one of the country’s most influential suicide prevention nonprofits. John Bennett is a NYC based comedian from Milford Connecticut, known for his high energy on stage and sharp witted observation humor. John’s comedic style involves a blend of personal storytelling and inherent goofiness, with an undercurrent of controlled rage. He has performed all over the US and is a local favorite among NYC comedy clubs. He currently co-produces "Tight Pants Comedy Show", which has been featured in TimeOutNY and the NY Comedy Festival.

When the credits roll, don’t go home. The night transforms into our ticketed Time Warp After Dark DJ Party, with DJ Dmitri keeping the dance floor moving late into the night. Come in costume, grab a drink, and keep doing the Time Warp with us!
WHEN
Saturday, October 24
Screening: 8:00 PM
Time Warp After Dark: Immediately following the film
WHERE
Industry City
Brooklyn, New York
ADMISSION
* Shadow-cast screening: FREE
* Frank-N-Furter Look-Alike Contest entry: $5
* Time Warp After Dark DJ Party: Separate ticket required
* Prop bags: Available for purchase
* Food by TACO MIX: Available for purchase all night
Come in costume, grab a prop bag and some tacos, and let the bkONE shadow cast guide you through a night dedicated to Rocky Horror, Tim Curry, and absolute pleasure.
We’re already trembling with antici…pation!

For the 8th year, City of Gods takes over Industry City for 2 breathtaking nights.
A city of endless potential.
A city of love and dust.
A city of revelry and renaissance.
Single day tickets + 2-day passes are available
Read the FAQ: www.cityofgods.nyc/faq
Come play in a massive labyrinth of stages, shrines, and sanctuaries designed for dance, play, pleasure, and expansive celebration. Express your extravagance at a gathering of immense opulence.
We welcome all deities, demigods and demons, goddexxes, creatures of creation and those devoted to hedonism beyond the human realm.
City of Gods features curated selection of Burning Man camps and creative visionaries to create our larger-than-life City.
